strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear failure cases; addresses genuine challenges in compositional T2V generation (semantic confusion, spatial misalignment, missing entities)
Training-free framework is practically significant—enables seamless integration with diverse T2V architectures without retraining or fine-tuning
Technical approach is sound with clear problem decomposition: Semantic Anchor Disambiguation (SAD) for semantic consistency and Dynamic Layout Fusion Attention (DLFA) for spatial-temporal binding
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple benchmarks (T2V-CompBench, VBench), 8+ metrics, comparisons with numerous baselines, and validation across models (CogVideoX, VideoCrafter2)
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 2-3) demonstrating the contribution of individual components and alternative design choices
Excellent presentation with clear figures, well-organized structure, and comprehensive supplementary material
Strong empirical results showing consistent improvements across multiple metrics and applications (complex prompts, trajectory-controllable generation)
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual components (semantic interpolation, attention-based layouts) are not fundamentally new; contribution is primarily engineering-focused

Ad-hoc design choices lack rigorous justification: cosine similarity for confusion scales, time-aware strength function ω(t) = 1 - t/τ, attention-correlation-based layout refinement all appear somewhat arbitrary without ablations

Incomplete experimental evaluation: (1) no user study despite relying on perceptual quality claims, (2) incomplete baseline comparisons (marked with '-'), (3) no quantitative metrics for trajectory control application

Missing critical reproducibility information: no mention of code release; inference time overhead claimed but not quantified; LLM prompt engineering details and model-specific tuning procedures under-specified
Scalability and boundary conditions not explored: no evaluation with >5 subjects, no analysis of failure modes for complex/ambiguous prompts, practical limits unclear

Theoretical justification lacking: no formal analysis of why these mechanisms ensure stated improvements, no convergence properties for iterative refinement, sensitivity analysis for key parameters absent
Heavy reliance on LLM-generated layouts introduces additional dependency; potential bottleneck for very complex scenarios not discussed

strengths: Addresses a real and challenging problem in compositional text-to-video generation with multiple subjects
Clear and well-structured dual-phase refinement approach with comprehensive figures and visual examples
Practical training-free design that leverages existing pre-trained models without finetuning
Evaluation on two established benchmarks (T2V-CompBench and VBench) with multiple metrics
Includes ablation studies demonstrating contribution of individual components (Tables 2-3)
Extensive supplementary material with implementation details and additional qualitative results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Semantic Anchor Disambiguation (SAD) is a straightforward embedding scaling based on confusion, and Dynamic Layout Fusion Attention (DLFA) is standard attention masking—neither represents a significant methodological advance
Modest empirical improvements without statistical validation: Table 1 shows typical gains of 1-3% (e.g., Consist-attr 0.6673→0.6713) without confidence intervals, significance tests, or multiple runs
No user studies or perceptual evaluation: All improvements claimed based on automatic metrics which have known limitations; subjective visual comparisons are insufficient
Misleading 'training-free' framing: Method depends entirely on pre-trained models; lacking finetuning is increasingly common in diffusion-based inference and not distinctive
Serious reproducibility concerns: No code availability mentioned, critical hyperparameters scattered across appendix, dependence on multiple pre-trained models not all publicly available
Unfair experimental comparisons: Different methods use different resolutions (512×320 vs 720×480), confounding factors not properly controlled, mixed open-source and proprietary baselines
Questionable design choices: Confusion scale formula (Eq. 1) lacks justification; why this specific weighting? Time-aware interpolation (Eq. 3) appears ad-hoc with no ablation
Limited scope and generalization: Specialized to compositional T2V; unclear how insights transfer to other domains or how methods scale to more complex scenarios
Baseline implementation concerns: Table 3 suggests some baseline implementations may be suboptimal, raising questions about fair comparison
No failure case analysis or discussion of limitations beyond brief supplementary section; cherry-picked qualitative examples without systematic evaluation

strengths: Training-free, architecture-agnostic framework that seamlessly integrates with multiple T2V models (CogVideoX, VideoCrafter2), significantly increasing practical applicability
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with consistent improvements across 8 metrics on established benchmarks (T2V-CompBench, VBench) and extensive qualitative comparisons against relevant baselines
Well-motivated dual-phase approach targeting specific, demonstrated problems in compositional T2V generation (semantic confusion, spatial misalignment, missing entities, attribute binding)
Clear technical presentation with effective visualizations, detailed architecture diagrams, and thorough ablation studies validating individual component contributions
Practical utility demonstrated through real-world applications including complex prompt-based and trajectory-controllable video generation scenarios
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—individual components (semantic anchor interpolation, LLM-guided layout masks, attention modulation) are relatively straightforward applications of existing techniques rather than fundamentally new algorithmic contributions

Insufficient theoretical justification for key design choices: why this specific confusion scale formulation (Eq. 1), why linear temporal attenuation ω(t)=1-t/T, and mechanistic understanding of why semantic confusion occurs

Critical dependency on external LLM (ChatGLM4) for layout generation creates reproducibility concerns, external failure points, and unclear robustness to LLM variations despite extensive prompt engineering details in supplementary material

Underspecified computational overhead: training-free inference still requires LLM calls and additional attention computations (16-21% overhead mentioned only in appendix); no detailed resource requirements or inference time comparisons provided
Modest performance improvements in several metrics (e.g., Consist-attr: 0.6873→0.6965, ≈1.3% gain) without statistical significance testing, leaving unclear perceptual meaningfulness to end users

Limited analysis of failure modes and limitations (Section 6)—acknowledges struggles with complex/ambiguous prompts but provides no concrete examples, systematic characterization, or guidance on applicability boundaries

Evaluation scope limitations: no user studies validating perceptual improvements, limited baseline comparisons (some from 2023-2024), and missing comparisons with recent compositional-specific methods; evaluation restricted to two benchmarks

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear articulation of two distinct challenges (subject presence and inter-subject relations) and elegant decoupling strategy
Strong empirical results with substantial improvements (15.7-29.84%) across multiple T2V models on T2V-CompBench and consistent outperformance of existing compositional methods
Broad generalizability demonstrated through seamless integration into diverse architectures (DiT, MM-DiT, U-Net) and extension to T2I generation
Comprehensive experimental validation including multiple benchmarks, thorough ablation studies with proper baseline reproductions, and detailed qualitative analysis
Practical design with training-free approach, only 5% inference overhead, and flexible IOU-guided attention modulation superior to rigid bbox masking
Transparent treatment of limitations with honest discussion of LLM layout planning errors and robustness mechanisms in appendices
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification for key design choices: saliency score formulation (Eq. 1) lacks deeper analysis of why cosine similarity captures semantic interference, temperature parameter τ=0.2 appears arbitrary, and time-aware function ω(t) is ad-hoc
External dependency on GPT-4o-mini API introduces non-trivial constraints: 5 second latency per prompt, API costs (~$0.005/request), and reproducibility limitations without API access
Modest improvements to general video quality on VBench (often <1% or negligible) raise questions about potential trade-offs between compositional and quality improvements

Incremental novelty: core components (semantic condition manipulation, soft attention modulation) are evolutionary refinements of prior work (ToMe/SEGA, VideoTetris/DreamRunner) rather than fundamentally new concepts

Incomplete analysis of LAM robustness: simple mean thresholding for adaptive layout generation (Eq. 5) lacks exploration of failure modes and interaction dynamics between LLM-planned and adaptive layouts

Gaps in experimental analysis: limited edge case exploration (complex scenes, many subjects), missing comparisons with some recent methods, heterogeneous baselines complicating direct component comparison

strengths: Addresses a concrete and important problem in compositional video generation with clear motivation and visualization of challenges (subject presence and inter-subject relations)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple base models (Wan, CogVideoX, VideoCrafter2), benchmarks (T2V-CompBench, VBench, T2I-CompBench), and consistent improvements on compositional metrics
Training-free and model-agnostic approach with minimal inference overhead (5%), making it practically applicable to existing video generation systems
Well-designed ablation studies (Tables 5-8) demonstrating contribution of each component and design choice
Seamless integration into diverse model architectures (DiT, MM-DiT, U-Net) with clear adaptation strategies
weaknesses: Critical dependency on external GPT-4o-mini API service undermines 'training-free' claim and raises fundamental reproducibility concerns; layout planning errors (1.14% error rate) and API dependency make results non-reproducible and method impractical for many users

Limited technical novelty: SCI is straightforward softmax-based saliency estimation and cosine similarity matching; LAM applies standard attention bias injection with IOU guidance; main contribution is engineering combination rather than technical innovation

Numerous unclear technical details that impede reproducibility: dimension specifications in Equations 1 and 3, softmax normalization in Equation 6, binary mask conversion for IOU in Equation 11, and missing justifications for design choices (τ=0.2, linear decay in ω(t))

Marginal improvements on general video quality: VBench quality score improves only +0.29% (Table 2) and T2I-CompBench improves 5.36%, far below T2V-CompBench gains; no user studies validating perceptual significance of improvements

Insufficient analysis of scope and limitations: only demonstrated on 2-4 subject prompts without evaluation on 5+ subjects; no concrete failure case examples; layout planning error impact on final quality not quantified; applicability boundaries not discussed

Large variance in improvements across base models (4.3% on Wan2.2 to 29.8% on CogVideoX) inadequately explained; raises questions about generalization and whether improvements are consistent or architecture-specific
No mention of code release or implementation availability; external API dependency creates barriers to reproducibility and practical adoption by the research community

strengths: Clear and intuitive problem decomposition via 'Present-and-Align' paradigm that effectively decouples subject presence (condition-level) from inter-subject relations (attention-level)

Comprehensive experimental validation across 4+ video models, 3 benchmarks, with fair baseline comparisons, thorough ablations, and convincing both quantitative (15.7% improvement on Wan2.1) and qualitative results
Training-free and broadly applicable approach requiring minimal modifications across different architectures (DiT, MM-DiT, U-Net) with only 5% inference overhead
Technically sound mathematical formulations for both SCI and LAM components; saliency-based adaptive interpolation more effective than fixed-weight alternatives
Demonstrates strong generalization to T2I tasks and outperforms training-based layout methods, showing broader applicability beyond T2V
Thorough appendices with implementation details, robustness analysis (LLM error rate reduction to 1.14%), and clear documentation of design choices
weaknesses: Insufficient theoretical or empirical justification for key design choices: saliency formula (Eq. 1) with τ=0.2, restoration vector formulation (Eq. 2), and 20% timestep cutoff lack ablations despite being important hyperparameters

Critical dependency on external LLM (GPT-4o-mini) for layout planning introduces cost, latency, and robustness concerns; while error rate reduced to 1.14%, paper lacks analysis of how Comp-Attn handles genuinely incorrect layouts

Claims of 'seamless integration' contradicted by architecture-specific adaptations required for MM-DiT and U-Net, suggesting method is architecture-aware rather than truly universal; critical details relegated to Appendix A
Limited failure mode analysis: no systematic study of challenging scenarios (dense scenes, unusual prompt structures, conflicting spatial relationships); failure discussion only in Appendix G
Modest or negligible improvements on VBench quality metrics, suggesting potential trade-offs between composition and general video quality that are not thoroughly explored

No code availability mentioned despite increasingly expected standard for reproducibility; hyperparameter sensitivity analysis missing; LLM API dependency may limit future reproducibility if models/pricing change
